title: Session synthesis: open-ended config probe and task flows
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Rapid synthesis from 6 moderated usability sessions (mixed remote and in-person) run Nov 4–9, 2025.
- Probe area: rollout & routing configuration flows + model selection affordances (how customers understand cost/latency trade-offs).
- Goal: identify common mental models, micro-friction points, and high-impact backlog items for Q1 roadmap.

Participants (summary):
- N = 6 (3 platform engineers, 2 ML engineers, 1 product manager).
- Companies: 2 startups, 3 mid-market SaaS, 1 internal solutions-eng pilot.
- Experience: ranged from 6 months to 7 years using LLM APIs; half had used Redwood Dedicated.

Test protocol (short):
1) Brief intro + warm-up (5m)
2) Think-aloud while configuring a canary rollout for a new LLM variant (20m)
3) Task: set up policy-based routing that prefers lower-cost variant under load (15m)
4) Probe: interpret per-route cost/latency estimates (10m)
5) Post-task SUS-style rating + open questions (5m)

Key quantitative signals (median):
- Task completion (canary setup): 5/6 completed; median time 12:30.
- Task completion (policy routing): 3/6 completed without help; median time 16:45.
- Confidence (1–5): canary 4.0, routing 2.8.
- SUS-style quick score: 68 (note: small N, directional only).

Top qualitative findings (high-level):
1) Canary setup flow is broadly understood but users expect clearer default safe values. Several skipped the "rollback" toggle because it was visually de-emphasized.
   - Quote: "I almost missed the rollback option — I assumed it would be automatic."
2) Policy-based routing mental model mismatch: participants expected a single slider for cost/latency tradeoff or presets (e.g., "cost-first", "latency-first"). The current multi-field rule builder felt like writing a policy language.
   - Observation: 4/6 tried to create a single rule; when prompted to add weight-based fallbacks they were unsure how weights interacted with batching.
3) Per-route cost/latency estimates are valuable but not trusted without provenance info. Users asked: "Where does this estimate come from? sample traces? avg tokens?"
4) Model catalog affordances: participants wanted to see estimated token unit price per model variant (normalized to a baseline) and a short expected latency band for typical sequence lengths.
5) Microcopy and labeling: terms like "variant", "fallback", and "route" were interpreted inconsistently. Several called out that "variant" sounded like model versioning but wasn't sure if it included quantization choices.

Observed friction points (specifics):
- Routing UI: rule builder lacks presets; weight-based controls unclear; missing preview of traffic split impact. (Severity: high)
- Canary defaults: rollback and exposure percent buried visually. Suggest promote defaults and a single-line summary at top. (Severity: medium)
- Cost provenance: tooltip/expandable section needed explaining how cost is estimated (batching assumptions, avg seq length). (Severity: medium)
- Model detail card: missing quick link to benchmark/throughput profile; participants wanted an at-a-glance expected qps for their hardware/region. (Severity: low)

Wireframe notes + quick sketches to iterate (engineer-friendly):
- Add "Preset" toggle in routing modal: presets = [Latency-first, Cost-first, Balanced, Conservative]. Selecting a preset adjusts underlying rule builder. (Owner: Marcus)
- Top summary bar in rollout modal: one-line human-readable summary (e.g., "Canary 10% -> 90% base, rollback: on, duration: 24h"). Persist summary after saving. (Owner: Elena)
- Cost provenance panel under per-route estimates: show source (historical traces OR simulator), assumptions (avg seq, caching enabled?), and confidence band. Link to "simulate" button. (Owner: Jordan)
- Model catalog quick metrics: token price normalized, latency band for 16/64/256 tokens, recommended usage patterns. (Owner: product data)

Backlog grooming (concrete tickets suggested):
- UX-4821: Routing presets + UI for toggling presets (epic) — split into: preset selector, preset->rule mapping, analytics hook.
- PLT-3317: Rollout summary top-bar and default rollback visibility (small story).
- ENG-5972: Cost estimator provenance endpoint + front-end panel (requires backend simulation endpoint).
- UX-4909: Model card quick metrics and benchmark link (design + data).
- UX-4918: Microcopy audit for terms: variant/fallback/route (content + glossary update).

Risks / open questions:
- Backend support: can we return simulator provenance within current SLAs? Need SRE/infra check (ENG-5972 dependency).
- Presets mapping: what exact parameters constitute a preset? (product + applied-ml to define).
- Analytics: how do we surface the impact of presets on cost forecast? instrumentation required.

Priority recommendations (actionable):
1) Short-term (next 2 weeks): implement rollup summary in rollout modal + promote rollback toggle (fast front-end changes). Owner: Elena.
2) Mid-term (Q1): implement routing presets + rules mapping; pair product + applied-ml to define presets. Owner: Marcus + Applied ML.
3) Research follow-up: run A/B with 12 participants comparing preset vs current rule builder for routing flows (metrics: success rate, time, subjective trust). Owner: Aisha.

Conference of notes:
- Cross-ref to previous console sessions: see Confluence UX-ROLL-2025 for prior probe on "model-selection" (linked). This session re-iterates demand for clear cost provenance.
- Slack tag for design prototypes: #console-ux — posted sketch v1 on 2025-11-14.

Appendix: session-level anecdotes (short):
- P1 (platform eng): tried to use tags in rule conditions to route by "team" — but the UI didn't expose tag hints; suggested autocomplete for metadata.
- P3 (ML eng): asked for a simulator button: "If I set this policy, what will my 95th percentile latency look like under 100 rps?"
- P5 (product): wanted guardrails: "If cost exceeds $X/day, alert me or automatically shift to cheaper variant."

Next steps and owners:
- Create the four JIRA tickets above and link to this doc (Aisha) — target: 2025-11-20.
- Quick prototype for rollout summary and rollback prominence (Elena) — show in design review 2025-11-25.
- Engineering feasibility for cost provenance (Marcus to sync with infra on 2025-11-18).

Unresolved/parking lot items:
- Should presets be editable? (pros/cons)
- How to show batched vs single-request cost assumptions in estimator UI.

Status and intended audience:
- Internal synthesis for product, applied-ml, and frontend eng. Not customer-facing.

Document notes: this is intentionally a working synthesis — contains verbatim participant quotes and quick-backlog suggestions. Treat as a draft; plan to refine into tickets with clear ACs before engineering kickoff.
